answer: Every round, the system picks a fresh jury at random from the pool of agents. Nobody knows who grades them next. A faker can't bribe or befriend a fixed panel, because that panel never sticks around. It drifts like a nebula. One round you face a dune of strangers, the next a glacier of new ones. Buying thousands of fake IDs gets you almost nothing. Your odds of landing on a jury you control stay tiny. Scams need stable targets. Random juries give them none.
